literal: For the help done without [the receiver] having done [any prior help], even the earth and even the heaven, matching [it], is rare.
translation: For a help rendered to one who has done no prior favor, even the earth and the heaven are not an equivalent recompense.
modern: முன்பு தான் எந்த உதவியும் செய்யாதிருந்தும் தனக்குச் செய்யப்பட்ட உதவிக்கு, மண்ணுலகத்தையும் விண்ணுலகத்தையும் கைம்மாறாகக் கொடுத்தாலும் ஈடாகாது.
explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme value of unsolicited or initial help. When someone assists us without us having done any prior favor to them, that act of kindness is priceless because it is born out of pure goodwill rather than obligation. The poet states that even gifting the entire earth and the heavens would not be a sufficient return to match such selfless help. The contrast between 'செய்யாமல்' (without doing) and 'செய்த' (done) emphasizes that the absence of a prior debt makes the received help infinitely valuable.
